// The control layer

Yourphone,answeredbyintention.

No menus, no hunting for a button. A small, natural finger motion is all it takes — Tactiq reads it on your hand and your phone simply responds.

One ringBluetooth LEOn-deviceHaptic feedback

Meet the ring

One feather-light smart ring on the index finger of either hand. Your thumb taps eight contact points on your own fingers — nine fixed commands you can always feel.

VoiceOverTalkBackOne-handedEyes-free

Augments your screen reader

Tactiq drives VoiceOver and TalkBack — it never replaces them. Confirm, go back, next, previous, read again, undo, two shortcuts, and a deliberate 5-second emergency hold.

Priced like earbudsNine commandsVoice setupNo screens

Built for independence

Positioned to be priced like earbuds, not like braille hardware — the bench prototype is under $60 in parts. A student research project, with every performance figure a pre-registered target.

Intention → action, in real time

How Tactiq works

01

Wake

The ring is idle until you deliberately squeeze its body. That squeeze opens a short command window — the design target is at most one false activation per hour.

02

Tap

Your thumb taps one of eight contact points — the tips and bases of your four fingers. Points you can always find, because they are part of your own hand.

03

Detect

The ring senses the tap privately on-device — a passive magnet and three small magnetometers, no camera, no microphone — then speaks to your phone over Bluetooth.

04

Execute

Your phone runs the command through VoiceOver or TalkBack — Tactiq augments the screen reader you already use, never replaces it.

05

Confirm

A distinct haptic pattern confirms what the ring heard. Nine fixed commands, always on your hand — the interface disappears and the control stays.

Accessibility shouldn't cost more than a laptop.

Braille displays run $799 to $15,500. Tactiq is positioned to be priced like earbuds — one ring, nine commands, and your phone back under your control. Join the waitlist to follow the research.
